data.title: Rheb GTPase is a direct target of TSC2 GAP activity and regulates mTOR signaling
data.authors: Inoki K; Li Y; Xu T; Guan KL

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: TSC2 is a GAP for Rheb; loss of TSC2 raises Rheb-GTP and constitutively activates mTOR.
data.abstract_excerpt: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a genetic disease caused by mutation in either TSC1 or TSC2. The TSC1 and TSC2 gene products form a functional complex and inhibit phosphorylation of S6K and 4EBP1. These functions of TSC1/TSC2 are likely mediated by mTOR. Here we report that TSC2 is a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) toward Rheb, a Ras family GTPase. Rheb stimulates phosphorylation of S6K and 4EBP1. This function of Rheb is blocked by rapamycin and dominant-negative mTOR.

extracted_findings.effect: TSC2 is a GAP for Rheb; Rheb-GTP activates mTOR/S6K/4EBP1 (rapamycin-sensitive)
